stage: STAGE 0 -- prior-art kill test, formal model, source-grounded conflict reproduction, set-valued feasibility

preserved_prior_verdicts.evidence-semantic checker: useful engineering tool, not dissertation novelty

claims.statement: Every component of the proposed architecture is established prior art in a separate literature: tolerating conflicting specifications (ViewPoints), set-valued interpretation under model ambiguity (credal sets / imprecise probability / DRO), implementations disagreeing on identical raw input (parser differentials / LangSec / ParDiff), and conflicting evidence in a safety argument (Dempster-Shafer safety-case confidence).
claims.evidence: PRIOR_ART_MATRIX.md. ViewPoints states 'tolerate inconsistency' as its organising principle (Hunter & Nuseibeh TSE 1994; Managing inconsistent specifications TOSEM 1998).
claims.assumptions: Snippet-level search; full-text retrieval blocked by the environment's egress policy for every scholarly host tried. Understates prior art if anything.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Each component is subsumed; the literal four-way conjunction was not found in one work.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Any suggestion that representing conflicting authorities without resolving them, or set-valued output, originates here.
claims.next_falsification_test: Search certification treatment (DO-178C, ISO 26262) of standards that are silent where implementations must choose.

claims.statement: Item 44's proposition -- a conclusion is robust iff F(C,w) = y for all C in the authority set -- is the textbook definition of robustness over an ambiguity set.
claims.evidence: Credal sets, imprecise probability, distributionally robust optimization. The brief predicts it is tautological.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: It is a definition, restated in a new vocabulary.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Calling it a result, a theorem, or a proposition of this work.

claims.statement: The battery disagreement reproduces exactly: 5.00 A, 0.00 A and -1.00 A into the same frozen core from one raw condition.
claims.evidence: Measured at the core boundary before anything else was built (item 51). Identical to research/evidence_semantics at 2036a2a.
claims.assumptions: Replay through committed decoders; no hardware.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Three committed decoders give one raw condition three different currents.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That this is evidence of semantic uncertainty rather than of three consumer bugs. S5 settles that.

claims.statement: The specification and the producer never disagree. Zero SPEC_VS_PRODUCER conflicts across all three cases.
claims.evidence: AUTHORITY_CONFLICTS.csv. Battery: MAVLink declares invalid="-1" and ArduPilot's GCS_Common.cpp:390-393 writes exactly -1 when it has no current -- the sole AGREEMENT row in that case is that pair. GNSS and mag: the spec is SILENT on the aspect the producer speaks to, so there is nothing to disagree with. 17 conflicts total: 8 CROSS_CONSUMER, 6 PRODUCER_VS_CONSUMER, 3 SPEC_VS_CONSUMER.
claims.assumptions: Producer authority read from the ArduPilot source tree at /home/user/ardupilot/ardupilot, not from a flying binary.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: There is no conflict between semantic authorities above the consumer. All disagreement is consumer-side.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That no such conflict could exist in any system. Three cases in one codebase.
claims.next_falsification_test: A field whose schema and producer genuinely disagree -- none was found here, and finding one would reopen the direction.

claims.statement: No authority disagreement in any of the three cases reaches the ACTION level. The failsafe issues an identical action set whichever consumer authority is chosen.
claims.evidence: DECISION_SENSITIVITY.csv: ACTION is ROBUST in all three cases. CONFLICT_PROPAGATION.csv: 0 of 9 authority pairs have disagreement reaching ACTION.
claims.assumptions: One word per case, the shortest that realises the raw state; a 15 s run; a null control at every level.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Item 29's NO_DECISION_RELEVANT_SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY holds at the action level for all three cases.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That no conflict anywhere could change an action. The search covered three cases and one word each.
claims.next_falsification_test: Longer words and a fault severe enough to drive battery trust below power_critical (0.70), which this run never reached.

claims.statement: The GNSS case is the only one whose disagreement reaches ASSURANCE, and even there only as timing: the level history and action set are identical.
claims.evidence: DECISION_SENSITIVITY.csv, gnss row: ASSURANCE SEMANTICALLY_AMBIGUOUS, ACTION ROBUST. The previous package measured the gap as 0.12-0.32 s of failsafe latency.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: The deepest consequence found anywhere is a failsafe latency difference, not a different decision.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: 'Changes failsafe behaviour' without the latency qualifier.

claims.statement: The MAVLink schema is SILENT about what GPS_RAW_INT.lat/lon/alt contain when fix_type < 3, and about the magnetometer all-zero triple. The consumers' divergent choices there are licensed, not violations.
claims.evidence: common.xml:GPS_RAW_INT.lat carries no `invalid=` attribute and no clause covering the no-fix case; SCALED_IMU.xmag likewise. ArduPilot fills the position fields with the last known Location (AP_GPS.cpp:1399-1417), which the spec permits because the spec did not speak.
claims.assumptions: The dialects searched: common, minimal, ardupilotmega, standard.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: This is UNDERSPECIFICATION, not conflict. Nobody is wrong because nobody said.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Counting these pairs as authority conflicts. Doing so would inflate 7 gaps into disagreements.
claims.next_falsification_test: Check whether a later MAVLink revision or a dialect extension fills the gap.

claims.statement: SILENT must be distinguished from an interpretation, or item 8's conflict definition miscounts every gap as a disagreement.
claims.evidence: conflicts.py. Item 8 defines conflict as |{C_a(r)}| > 1; encoding silence as an interpretation would make 7 UNDERSPECIFICATION pairs read as CONFLICT.
claims.assumptions: Follows from the definition; it is a modelling observation, not a measurement.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: The conflict/underspecification distinction is necessary for the count to mean anything.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That the distinction is new. Incompleteness versus inconsistency is a named axis in the multi-perspective requirements literature.
claims.next_falsification_test: Read the ViewPoints incompleteness papers in full; they very likely make this distinction already.

claims.statement: SPEC_FIRST resolves 2 of 3 cases and fails only where the spec is SILENT; IMPLEMENTATION_FIRST resolves 2 of 3; OBSERVATION_FIRST resolves 0 of 3.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Spec precedence is sufficient wherever the spec speaks; where it is silent no precedence rule applies, because there is no higher authority to defer to.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: SPEC_PRECEDENCE_SUFFICIENT as the overall verdict -- it fails 1 of 3.
claims.next_falsification_test: More cases where the schema is silent; the previous package measured 91 of 106 MAVLink fields with no `invalid=` attribute, so silence is the common case.

claims.statement: Set-valued output flags ambiguity at upstream levels but in 0 of 3 cases does that ambiguity reach ACTION.
claims.evidence: results/BASELINE_SUMMARY.json: ambiguity rate 0.389, robust rate 0.333, confounded 0.278 over 18 case-level cells; cases_where_B3_ambiguity_reaches_ACTION = 0.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: On these cases the extra information set-valued output carries changes nothing the vehicle would do.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: SET_VALUED_OVERKILL as a general claim. Three cases cannot establish that.
claims.next_falsification_test: A case where a conflict reaches ACTION; none was found.

claims.statement: Almost a third of the level cells are CONFOUNDED_BY_CONTROL: the three paths already disagree on an all-nominal word.
claims.evidence: results/BASELINE_SUMMARY.json, confounded_rate 0.278. The DIAGNOSIS level is confounded in all three cases.
claims.assumptions: The null control is V^k at the same length.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Without the control, DIAGNOSIS-level disagreement would have been reported as authority conflict in all three cases. It is a sample-rate and timestamp artifact.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Reporting the raw distinct-outcome counts without the control column.
claims.next_falsification_test: Equalise the sample rates across paths and see whether the DIAGNOSIS confound disappears.

claims.statement: The conflicts are removable by ordinary engineering: make the three consumers honour the agreed authority, and where no authority speaks, decide and write it down.
claims.evidence: S4 (no authority conflict above the consumer) plus S7 (the residue is a specification gap). Item 52's test.
claims.assumptions: The fixes were NOT implemented. Item 51 requires the research branch to retain pre-fix behaviour, so this is an analytic argument from the authority table, not a measured before/after.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Every counted conflict is attributable to a consumer choice that a fix would remove, and the remainder is a gap a decision would close.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That the fixes were applied and the conflicts measured to disappear. They were not.
claims.next_falsification_test: Implement the three fixes on a separate branch and re-run conflicts.py; item 52 predicts the conflict count drops to zero.

claims.statement: Two modelling errors of mine inflated the conflict count before they were caught.
claims.evidence: (1) C_producer_absence describes a DIFFERENT raw state (no GPS configured) and was pooled into the no-fix resolution, making IMPLEMENTATION_FIRST read as SELF_INCONSISTENT on GNSS. (2) C_spec speaks about what fix_type MEANS while C_producer speaks about what the position fields CONTAIN; comparing them produced a spurious SPEC_VS_PRODUCER conflict. Both fixed by adding explicit `scope` and `aspect` coordinates; both recorded in AUTHORITY_MODEL.md rather than silently repaired.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: The headline finding -- zero SPEC_VS_PRODUCER conflicts -- exists only after correcting a category error that had manufactured one.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Presenting the corrected count without the correction.
claims.next_falsification_test: Re-derive aspects from the schema field names mechanically rather than by hand.

claims.statement: The citation verifier caught five bad citations in the first run of the authority table, including one of my own line numbers and four schema locators written as placeholders.
claims.evidence: authorities.py:verify(). ardupilot.py:143 was wrong (the line is 146), and every common.xml citation used a line number where a MESSAGE.field locator was needed.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Every authority citation in AUTHORITY_TABLE.csv is re-read from disk and 16 of 16 now verify.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: That the table was right first time.
claims.next_falsification_test: Re-run authorities.py; it exits non-zero if any citation stops resolving.

claims.statement: No physical HIL was performed and no hardware is connected.
claims.evidence: pyserial enumerates only /dev/ttyS0. PHYSICAL_AUTHORITY_VALIDATION_PLAN.md specifies what would be needed.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: The producer authority was read from source; nothing confirms the flying binary behaves the same way.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Any claim about physically observed interface semantics.
claims.next_falsification_test: Level 1 of the plan: emulator into a physical flight controller.

claims.statement: Assurance under conflicting semantic authorities is a novel research direction.
claims.assumptions: Snippet-level prior-art search; three cases in one codebase.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Not established. The authorities do not conflict, the consumer disagreements do not reach the action level, and every component of the machinery is prior art.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: novel, first, new paradigm, unprecedented, new theorem.
claims.next_falsification_test: A field where schema and producer genuinely disagree AND the disagreement changes a failsafe action. Neither half was observed here.

refuted_predictions.prediction: The battery three-way split is evidence of conflicting semantic authorities.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. The spec and the producer agree exactly; all three consumers disagree with that agreed authority. It is three bugs, not a conflict.

refuted_predictions.prediction: The GNSS case would show a specification-versus-producer conflict.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. The specification is SILENT on the position fields, so the producer contradicts nothing. The first version of the classifier reported a conflict here and was wrong.

refuted_predictions.prediction: At least one authority conflict would change a downstream assurance decision.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. 0 of 9 pairs reach ACTION. The deepest consequence is a failsafe latency difference.

not_done: No dissertation chapter, no paper, no novelty claim (item 61).
No security exploit tooling (item 48); SECURITY_IMPLICATIONS_NOTES.md is conceptual only.
No engineering fixes applied -- item 51 requires the research branch to retain pre-fix behaviour, so S12 is analytic rather than measured.
No PX4 producer-side reading (item 41); the prediction is recorded in CROSS_PLATFORM_FEASIBILITY.md instead.
No ambiguity-exposure integral (item 31): with one word per case there is no time series to integrate, and a number computed from three points would be decoration.
